spec.description: Retrieve methods available for depositing a particular asset. Requires the `Funds permissions - Query` and `Funds permissions - Deposit` API key permissions.

aclass.description: Asset class (optional). Only `currency` is broadly used today; `tokenized_asset` covers xstocks-style tokenized equities.

rebase_multiplier.description: Optional parameter for viewing xstocks data. `rebased` displays in terms of underlying equity; `base` displays in terms of SPV tokens.

response.description: Deposit methods available for the requested asset.

items.title: DepositMethod
items.description: One method available for depositing a particular asset.

method.description: Name of the deposit method, e.g. `Bitcoin`.

limit.description: Maximum net amount that can be deposited right now, or `false` if there is no limit.

fee.description: Amount of fees that will be paid (flat fee).

fee-percentage.description: Percentage fee that will be paid (used instead of `fee` for some methods, e.g. Lightning).

address-setup-fee.description: Whether or not the method has an address setup fee.

gen-address.description: Whether new addresses can be generated for this method.

minimum.description: Minimum net amount that can be deposited right now.

notes: Upstream `requestBody` requires `nonce`; dropped from this schema since the core's `authed_request` (`core/transport/http.py`) injects a strictly-increasing nonce into every private call automatically -- it is never a caller-supplied parameter, matching the existing hand-written `deposit_methods(self, asset)` signature, which takes none.

Upstream declares `gen-address`, `fee-percentage`, and `address-setup-fee` on the `DepositMethod` schema, none of which are valid Python identifiers -- the hand-written PoC `TypedDict` in `pkg/src/kraken/spot/funding.py` drops all three for that reason (see `spec/core.md` Gotchas). Kept here since a JSON Schema property name has no such constraint; real codegen should alias them to valid identifiers (e.g. `gen_address`).
`limit` has no `type` declared upstream ("... or false if no limit"); typed as `anyOf[string, boolean-literal-false]` to match the hand-written core's `str | Literal[False]`.

`fee` is required despite upstream's own prose implying it's replaced by `fee-percentage` for some methods (e.g. Lightning): live capture of `asset=XBT` (`examples/xbt`) shows `Bitcoin Lightning` returning both `fee: "0"` and `fee-percentage: "0.3"` simultaneously, and `fee` is present on 29/29 real methods observed across `asset=USDC` and `asset=XBT` -- trusting the live data over the docs' either/or phrasing, per docs/spec/authoring.md rule 8's own precedent.

`address-setup-fee` and `limit`'s string branch (vs. its `false` variant) are left as bare `string`, not `decimal-string`: no captured example across `asset=USDC`/`XBT` ever shows either as anything but absent (`address-setup-fee`) or `false` (`limit`), so there is no real value to confirm they're actually decimal-shaped -- rule 2/15's 'never invent' discipline applies the same way to a format as to an enum.
